messages:
sarah: hey team, first morning! my company MBP (M1, macOS 12.6) finished the MDM enrollment flow but the console shows FileVault NOT enabled and the device is flagged as non-compliant. When I try to enable FV from System Prefs it errors 'Unable to enable FileVault: no secure token users'. anyone seen this?

it-support: welcome :wave: yes, that's usually because the primary account doesn't have a SecureToken. Did you migrate your account from iCloud or restore from a Time Machine backup?

sarah: i restored from my personal backup before returning it to company image. didn't think that would matter.

luis: hi sarah — quick check: can you run `sudo fdesetup status` and `sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus $(whoami)` and paste outputs?

sarah: outputs below:
```
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.

$ sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus sarah
Secure token is DISABLED for user sarah
```

enrollment-bot: Enrollment record: serial=C02YQ9XXXXX user=sarah profile=redwood-mdm state=ENROLLED compliance=FDE_NOT_PROVISIONED

it-support: yup. The MDM expects a SecureToken user so it can escrow recovery keys. We'll need to create or use an existing SecureToken-enabled admin to grant sarah a token. Do you have any other local admin on that machine?

sarah: no, sarah is the only account. I do have my personal Apple ID admin on my old laptop, but not here.

luis: ok two safe options: 1) we create a one-time local admin account via our DEP/MDM command and use it to grant SecureToken to your user, then remove it; or 2) you can boot to Recovery and run the `resetpassword` utility to create a secure token-enabled user if company policy allows. We prefer option 1 since no reboot. Which do you want?

sarah: prefer not to reboot. can you create the temp admin?

it-support: proceeding with option 1. we'll push a temporary local admin named rdw-temp-admin that expires in 2 hours. we'll also open a screen share to guide you through password prompts.

enrollment-bot: MDM command: CreateLocalAdmin rdw-temp-admin issued to serial=C02YQ9XXXXX at 10:12 PT

luis: remote in. please open Terminal and run: `sudo sysadminctl -addUser rdw-temp-admin -fullName "Temp Admin" -password TempPass!234 -admin`

sarah: ran it and got prompt for my password (it asked for an admin to authorize). i entered mine and it accepted.

luis: great. now from the temp admin session run: `sudo sysadminctl -secureTokenOn sarah -password <sarah_password> -adminUser rdw-temp-admin -adminPassword TempPass!234`

sarah: doing that now. it prompted for my password. command returned no output but exit 0.

sarah: re-checking status:
```
$ sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus sarah
Secure token is ENABLED for user sarah
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
```

it-support: good, SecureToken granted. Next step: enable FileVault and let MDM escrow. From your account run `sudo fdesetup enable -user sarah` and follow prompts.

sarah: ran `sudo fdesetup enable -user sarah` — it asked for sarah's password and then showed a long recovery key. MDM bot just posted: `Recovery_key_received serial=C02YQ9XXXXX status=SUCCESS`

enrollment-bot: Compliance update: serial=C02YQ9XXXXX compliance=COMPLIANT FDE=MANAGED

luis: we'll remove rdw-temp-admin in a minute. double-check that Okta device-attestation popup appears (device trust).

sarah: got device trust prompt and completed it. web console now shows 'Disk encryption: Managed, Escrowed' and compliance green. huge thanks!

it-support: awesome. housekeeping: rdw-temp-admin will be deleted by MDM in 30 minutes. if you notice any odd prompts or missing home permissions after removal ping us.

sarah: will do. Appreciate the fast help :heart:
